{"text":"MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The dual-band TP-Link extender feels like a useful upgrade to my older N300 extender because it improves an existing setup and adds an Ethernet port.",
    "The Anker power strip fits my collection of desk devices: its longer cord and built-in USB charging offer a practical reason to add it.",
    "The Echo Dot and mesh system relate to my Alexa and networking purchases, even though that connection alone does not give me a reason to buy them now."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "The Galaxy Buds case, replacement antennas, and Android Auto adapter depend on equipment compatibility that my history does not establish.",
    "Another Echo Dot or photo display feels redundant after my recent Dot and Echo Show purchases; familiarity does not mean I need another device with the same purpose.",
    "The wired headphones and phone cables do not address a current need I recognize from my recent purchases."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My electronics purchases seem to have been treated as interest in almost any electronic accessory, even when I have no apparent use for it.",
    "Buying a device seems to have been taken as a reason to suggest another similar device, without considering whether the original purchase already met my need.",
    "My older GPS and networking purchases seem to imply compatibility with newer car accessories or specialized antennas, which I would need to verify."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My recent Alexa purchases make compatible additions relevant, but also reduce my immediate need for another speaker or display.",
    "I respond more strongly to a specific improvement, such as dual-band networking or convenient desk charging, than to a broad connection with electronics.",
    "A modest upgrade to equipment I already use is easier to justify than replacing my whole network with three mesh units without an established coverage need."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations recognize my interest in connected home devices and computer accessories, but miss the distinction between a useful upgrade, a duplicate, and an accessory requiring equipment I may not own."
}"}
